idiom_name: typed fetch middleware + branded IdempotencyKey (crypto.randomUUID); only replay-safe operations are typed as retryable
implementation_notes: There is no framework to install here; the TypeScript idiom is a small typed wrapper that owns the key: a branded type (type IdempotencyKey = string & { readonly __brand: "IdempotencyKey" }) so a key cannot be confused with any other string, one minting function (crypto.randomUUID(), present in browsers and Node), and a request helper whose retry option is accepted only for operations the types mark as replay-safe. That type-level distinction replaces the classic wrapper: a caller who wants retries on a create call must pass an IdempotencyKey and gets the header for free, while an unkeyed POST does not type-check against the retrying client. Runtime behaviour still comes from the platform or a library (fetch plus a retry helper), so the wrapper stays thin.
pitfalls: A key typed as plain string is reasoned about as a value rather than a capability; branding it and minting it once is what keeps a retry from silently re-minting it.
Types cannot stop the runtime from re-minting, so keep the key in the caller's pending-work record (IndexedDB/localStorage for offline clients) and pass it into the retry closure.
crypto.randomUUID() is unavailable in non-secure contexts, so a feature-detected fallback must still use a CSPRNG rather than Math.random().
